To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a new assay for detecting apoptotic circulating tumor cells (M30 CTC) in epithelial cancer patients, which may provide new information for the monitoring of response to anticancer therapy in clinical trials.

the M30 neo-epitope is detectable on circulating tumor cells, that the fraction of M30+ CTC varies among patients, and that the M30 CIC assay may be used as an additional marker of response in patients undergoing therapy.
we have developed a new method to quantify apoptotic CTC in the blood of cancer patients and that we have demonstrated the potential of this assay in a pilot clinical trial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new assay for quantifying the apoptotic fraction in circulating tumor cells (apoptosis CTC).
the identification of new biomarkers that can be used to monitor tumor progression in cancer patients

the development of new diagnostic tests based on the detection of circulating tumor cells (1, 2) and the quantification of apoptosis in CTC by means of a novel assay based on the detection by immunofluoroscent microscopy of a neoepitopes generated in early apoptosis of the cytokeratin 8/18 family of intermediate filament proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M30-positive cells are not necessarily apoptotic cells, as the M30 epitope is also present in necrotic and autophagic cells.
the M30 CIC assay is not ready for routine clinical use.

M30 expression on circulating tumor cells is a promising marker of apoptosis, which may be useful for monitoring dynamic changes of apoptotic tumor cells in the peripheral blood of patients with solid epithelial cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

M30 expression on circulating tumor cells is detectable by flow cytometry and the M30-integrated assay has potential for monitoring the dynamic changes in the ratio of apoptotic CCT to evaluate response in early phase clinical trials of molecular targeted anticancer therapeutcs as well as for the translational research, where there is a pressing nead for informative circulating biomakers.
we developed a method to detect and quantify apoptotic CTC.
we have developed and validated a method to measure the fraction of apoptotic circulating tumor cells (apoptotic CTC).
The main takeaway from our work is that
M30 expression is detectable on CTC, and that this may have a role in monitoring dynamic changes in apoptotic CTC during disease course and in response to treatment.
we were able to develop an assay to detect the M-30 neoepitopes in circulating tumor cells (1, 2).
the M30 assay is a useful addition to CellSearch analysis for monitoring the dynamics of CTCs in patients with cancer.
